title: Fraxinellone mitigates acute lung injury by targeting HIF-1alpha to suppress pyroptosis and inflammation.
authors: Zhang, Bing; Lu, Xiaoning; Zhang, Yuefei; Shen, Xinyu; Tan, Zhongbing; Leng, Junling; Chen, Yifei; Shen, Hui; Li, Yong
one_liner_zh: 该文研究天然化合物Fraxinellone通过靶向HIF-1alpha抑制肺损伤中的焦亡和炎症，仅涉及分子对接且对象为蛋白-小分子，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: PURPOSE: Acute pulmonary contusion (APC), a life-threatening trauma-associated condition, currently lacks targeted pharmacological therapies. Fraxinellone (FRA) inhibits Hypoxia-inducible factor-1alpha (HIF-1alpha) synthesis, but its binding mechanism and anti-APC action remain unclear. This study was designed to assess the therapeutic potential of FRA, a natural substance with known anti-inflammatory properties, as a means of attenuating APC progression through the inhibition of HIF-1alpha. METHODS: An in vivo APC model was generated via weight-drop lung injury in C57BL/6 mice, and an in vitro model was established using thrombin (THR)-injured MLE-12 cells. The efficacy of FRA (10 muM in vitro; 5 mg/kg in vivo) was evaluated through cell viability assays, measurement of inflammatory cytokines via enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), histopathological examination, and molecular analyses including Western blot (WB) and real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). Mechanistic validation was performed through HIF-1alpha siRNA knockdown and mutation, ML228-mediated activation, and molecular docking simulations. RESULTS: FRA notably diminished APC severity by reducing pulmonary edema (wet/dry ratio), lowering pro-inflammatory cytokine levels ((interleukin-1beta [IL-1beta], interleukin-6 [IL-6], interleukin-18 [IL-18]), and decreasing pyroptosis markers (NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain containing 3 [NLRP3], gasdermin D [GSDMD]) in both in vitro and in vivo models. Molecular docking revealed FRA binding to HIF-1alpha at Arg258, and HIF-1alpha activation abrogated the protective effects of FRA. HIF-1alpha knockdown and mutation reproduced the anti-pyroptotic effects of FRA, confirming pathway specificity. CONCLUSION: FRA mitigates APC progression by targeting HIF-1alpha to suppress NLRP3/GSDMD-mediated pyroptosis and inflammation, providing a novel therapeutic approach for trauma-induced lung injury.
abstract_zh: 目的：急性肺挫伤（APC）是一种危及生命的创伤相关疾病，目前缺乏靶向药物治疗。梣酮（FRA）抑制缺氧诱导因子-1α（HIF-1α）的合成，但其结合机制及抗APC作用尚不清楚。本研究旨在评估FRA（一种具有已知抗炎特性的天然物质）通过抑制HIF-1α来减轻APC进展的治疗潜力。方法：通过C57BL/6小鼠重量跌落肺损伤建立体内APC模型，并使用凝血酶（THR）损伤的MLE-12细胞建立体外模型。通过细胞活力测定、酶联免疫吸附试验（ELISA）检测炎症细胞因子、组织病理学检查以及分子分析（包括蛋白质印迹（WB）和实时定量聚合酶链反应（RT-qPCR））评估FRA（体外10 μM；体内5 mg/kg）的疗效。通过HIF-1α siRNA敲低和突变、ML228介导的激活以及分子对接模拟进行机制验证。结果：FRA显著减轻APC严重程度，表现为降低肺水肿（湿/干比）、降低促炎细胞因子水平（白细胞介素-1β [IL-1β]、白细胞介素-6 [IL-6]、白细胞介素-18 [IL-18]），并在体外和体内模型中减少焦亡标志物（NOD样受体家族含pyrin结构域蛋白3 [NLRP3]、gasdermin D [GSDMD]）。分子对接显示FRA与HIF-1α在Arg258位点结合，且HIF-1α激活消除了FRA的保护作用。HIF-1α敲低和突变重现了FRA的抗焦亡效应，确认了通路特异性。结论：FRA通过靶向HIF-1α抑制NLRP3/GSDMD介导的焦亡和炎症，从而减轻APC进展，为创伤性肺损伤提供了一种新的治疗策略。
